headline: 英國作家推薦學校選書
context: 英國換了新首相后，《衛報》邀請多位作家推薦學校應該教的小說，包括班．奧克瑞（Ben Okri）與莎曼莎．哈維（Samantha Harvey）。另一篇報導則分享一部巴西紀錄片，如何啟發作者投入用音樂幫助青少年的公益工作。

sources.name: The Guardian
sources.summary: A new term, a new PM … time for a new English curriculum? We ask writers from Ben Okri to Samantha Harvey to pick books that will inspire a lifelong love of reading For the first time ever, we have a British prime minister who studied for an English degree. Not all of his 58 predecessors went to university, but those who did favoured subjects such as history and classics and, more recently, philosophy, politics and economics. Yet reading fiction is a fantastic preparation for life, for understanding people and the times through which we live. Novels encourage empathy, they help you to stand in other people’s shoes, to navigate complicated, sometimes conflicting emotions, they entertain and bring joy. The creative industries contribute some £145.8bn each year to the UK economy; it is our soft superpower. In other words, books matter. Reading matters. Continue reading...

sources.name: The Guardian
sources.summary: Favela Rising showed me how a grassroots movement can change the lives of young people. Its ethos is baked into the youth charity I work for – and where two of Ezra Collective met • ‘Like painting with light’: photographer Temi Adegbayibi on capturing the energy of music I grew up in Great Yarmouth listening to classical music, learning piano and violin, playing in an orchestra and singing the Beatles in choir. Music was something that was arranged and formal, a privilege handed to me. At 18 I moved to London to study it at university. But outside my small town, I quickly realised that I didn’t have what it took to make it as a performer. There were, however, two course units that really resonated with me: music therapy and music in cultural industries. They weren’t about being a musician but about using music in the wider world. And so, as graduation approached, I determined that if I could build a career in organisations that helped people through music, that would be a valuable way to pass on the opportunities I’d been given to others. thread_text:
英國換了會讀英文系的首相后，《衛報》邀請多位作家推薦學校應該教的小說，包括班．奧克瑞（Ben Okri）與莎曼莎．哈維（Samantha Harvey）。報導提到，英國創意產業每年為經濟貢獻約 1458 億英鎊，是英國的軟實力之一。另一篇專欄則分享，一部巴西紀錄片《Favela Rising》如何啟發作者，從小鎮學古典樂的孩子，走上用音樂幫助青少年的公益之路。

—— 本則整理自 The Guardian 於 2026 年 9 月 5 日發佈的報導，讓圖書館員翻譯給你聽。

voice_text: 英國換了會讀英文系的首相，衛報就找作家們推薦學校該教的小說。這次邀來的作家包括班．奧克瑞和莎曼莎．哈維。報導提到，英國創意產業每年貢獻經濟大約 1458 億英鎊——換算台幣大概5.8兆左右，是英國的軟實力之一。另一篇專欄則說，一部巴西紀錄片啟發了作者，從小鎮學古典樂的孩子，後來走上用音樂幫助青少年的公益之路。
